messages:
Maya: customer reports immediate 401s with `invalid_api_key` after copying an API key into their app this morning. says key previously worked. sample curl they sent (redacted):
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \n  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_************\" \n  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"hi"}'
```
Maya: they tried from both Node and curl, same 401. No rate-limit headers. region: us-east-1. Can someone advise quick repro steps to ask them?
Kevin: ask them to print the raw bytes of the key. lots of copy/paste issues add tabs or control chars. quick commands to send back:
```
# show nonprintables as hex (bash)
echo -n \"$API_KEY\" | xxd -p
# or to show escaped chars
echo -n \"$API_KEY\" | sed -n l
```
Kevin: if they see `09` (tab) or `0a`/`0d` (newline/CR) around the key that's the culprit. also common when copying from TSV/exported spreadsheet — tabs sneak in.
Maya: sent those commands. customer replied with output: `736b5f6c6976655f616263090a` (they pasted the hex) — looks like a tab (09) and newline (0a) appended. :face_with_monocle:
Alex: can confirm the auth check does a strict string match; additional bytes will cause validation to fail and we return 401. no partial-match policy.
Kevin: recommend their quick fix (two options):
```
# 1) strip tabs/newlines client-side
clean_key=$(echo -n \"$KEY\" | tr -d '\t\r\n')
# 2) safer: show bytes & copy exact hex, or re-generate a key from console
```
Kevin: also suggested a server-side improvement: return a more descriptive error when header contains non-ASCII control bytes in the token (filed a tiny follow-up)
Maya: customer applied `tr -d '\t\r\n'` and requests started working again. they said they had exported keys from an internal TSV and one cell had a trailing tab.
Maya: relayed fix and steps to avoid (copy from the console UI, or use `curl`/SDK sample that trims). they asked if we could detect common paste issues in our docs — filing doc request.
SupportBot: Ticket created: INC-12345. Escalation: assigned to Kevin for follow-up on better error message and doc update.
Kevin: I'll add a small doc blurb in `auth.md` and open a tiny runtime change to catch control bytes and return a clearer error code. :+1:
Alex: nice reproduction. closing thread after doc + small PR.
